newsitem.title: UK: UK ups wheat crop to 16 mln T, feed use higher.
newsitem.headline: UK ups wheat crop to 16 mln T, feed use higher.

text.p: The UK Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries (MAFF) on Wednesday revised up its estimate for wheat production by 186,000 tonnes to 16.041 million tonnes.

But it said the rise was offset by increased demand by the animal feed sector which was estimated to use over six million tonnes of wheat in the current 1996/97 (July/June) season -- a 10 year high -- according to a report issued by the Home-Grown Cereals Authority (HGCA).
MAFF reduced its UK barley output estimate to a final 7.765 million tonnes from its latest provisional estimate of 7.862 million tonnes.
Export availability of wheat, consisting of exportable surplus and intervention stocks, was put at 4.2 million tonnes with about 2.2 million tonnes estimated to have been exported to end-December.

"As feed wheat is not directly supported by intervention, wheat prices will have to remain competitive in order to move the two million tonne export availability for the second half of the season and prevent a large carryover in the industry," commented the HGCA.
Barley exports to end-December were pegged at 1.3 million tonnes, leaving one million tonnes exportable surplus for the rest of the season.

Intervention offers were likely, but in view of green sterling's expected revaluation on January 21, any large offers should have already occurred, the HGCA said. But so far only 10,000 tonnes had been offered.
MAFF's rapeseed harvest estimate was lowered to 1.45 million tonnes, still a record high, but despite the bumper crop rapeseed crushings were forecast to fall this season, the HGCA said.
